Borrowed from French bulletin. By surface analysis, bull (“ball”) + -et (“diminutive”) + -in (“diminutive”).

senses.d: A short report, especially one released through official channels to be immediately broadcast or publicized.
ex: A company bulletin announced changes to the policy.

senses.d: A time-sensitive news item or short news report.
ex: The evening news bulletin reported on the earthquake.

senses.d: A short printed publication, especially one produced regularly by an organization.
To announce (something) by means of such a report or publication.
ex: to bulletin an employment vacancy

senses.d: Introduces a fact (presumed to be obvious) of which the person addressed is ostensibly not aware.

ety.text: From Old French bullette + diminutive suffix -in, or possibly a borrowing from Italian bollettino.
From boleta (“receipt, bill, ticket”) + -ín, or a borrowing of equivalent Italian bollettino (“bulletin”). In both cases, from Italian bolletta (“receipt, bill”).
Compare French bulletin.
Deverbal from avisar.
